question: How far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: 30 feet
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 50 feet
choice_d: 20 feet
explanation: The manual states danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: Within the 30-foot danger zone in front of a school bus, which portion is the most dangerous?
choice_a: The last 10 feet
choice_b: The first 10 feet
choice_c: The middle 10 feet
choice_d: The entire zone equally
explanation: The manual specifies the first 10 feet of the front danger zone is the most dangerous.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: Why does the manual say the area to the left of a school bus is always considered dangerous?
choice_a: Because of the tail swing
choice_b: Because of the exhaust system
choice_c: Because of passing cars
choice_d: Because of blind spots created by mirrors
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: How far does the danger zone extend from the left/right sides and behind the rear bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 15 feet
choice_c: 20 feet
choice_d: 10 feet
explanation: Danger zones extend 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus and 10 feet behind the rear bumper.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.1 - Danger Zones

question: The outside left and right side flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see how far behind the bus?
choice_a: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths
choice_b: 100 feet or 2 bus lengths
choice_c: 300 feet or 6 bus lengths
choice_d: 50 feet or 1 bus length
explanation: The manual states the flat mirrors should allow the driver to see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.3 - Outside Flat Mirrors

question: Besides distance behind the bus, what else should the outside flat mirrors be adjusted to show?
choice_a: The engine compartment
choice_b: The rear tires touching the ground
choice_c: The stop arm
choice_d: The interior of the bus
explanation: Flat mirrors should show the rear tires touching the ground and along the sides of the bus.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.3 - Outside Flat Mirrors

question: What is the purpose of the outside left and right side convex mirrors?
choice_a: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_b: To see the front bumper danger zone
choice_c: To monitor the left and right sides of the bus at a wide angle
choice_d: To view the interior emergency exit
explanation: Convex mirrors provide a wide-angle view of traffic, clearances, and students at the side of the bus.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.4 - Outside Convex Mirrors

question: What limitation do the convex mirrors have, according to the manual?
choice_a: They cannot be used at night
choice_b: They must be replaced every year
choice_c: They only work when the bus is stopped
choice_d: They present a view that does not accurately reflect the size and distance of objects
explanation: Convex mirrors distort the apparent size and distance of people and objects, so the driver must account for this.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.4 - Outside Convex Mirrors

question: What is the purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors?
choice_a: To see the front bumper "danger zone" area not visible by direct vision
choice_b: To monitor passengers inside the bus
choice_c: To check tire tread wear
choice_d: To view the exhaust system
explanation: Crossover mirrors let the driver see the danger zone directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.5 - Crossover Mirrors

question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror mounted on a school bus?
choice_a: On the dashboard near the steering wheel
choice_b: Directly above the windshield on the driver's side
choice_c: On the rear emergency door
choice_d: At the left front corner of the bus
explanation: The manual states this mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver's side area of the bus.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.6 - Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: What is the overhead inside rearview mirror primarily used for?
choice_a: Viewing traffic behind the bus at a wide angle
choice_b: Checking tire pressure
choice_c: Monitoring passenger activity inside the bus
choice_d: Viewing the front bumper danger zone
explanation: The overhead inside mirror is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.6 - Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: Before operating a school bus, what should the driver do regarding mirrors?
choice_a: Adjust them only after the route begins
choice_b: Rely solely on the interior mirror
choice_c: Skip mirror checks if running on schedule
choice_d: Check each mirror to obtain maximum viewing area
explanation: The manual requires checking each mirror before operating the bus to obtain maximum viewing area.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.1.2 - Correct Mirror Adjustment

question: According to the manual, more students are killed each year:
choice_a: Getting on or off a school bus than as passengers inside one
choice_b: As passengers inside a school bus than getting on or off
choice_c: While crossing railroad tracks than at bus stops
choice_d: In bus stop parking lots than on the roadway
explanation: The manual states more students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside one.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2 - Loading and Unloading

question: When may a school bus driver change the location of a bus stop?
choice_a: At the driver's own discretion
choice_b: Only with written approval from the appropriate school district official
choice_c: Whenever weather conditions require it
choice_d: After informing students verbally
explanation: The manual states a driver should never change the location of a bus stop without written approval from the appropriate school district official.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: If equipped, when should alternating flashing amber warning lights be activated when approaching a stop?
choice_a: Only after coming to a complete stop
choice_b: At least 50 feet before the stop
choice_c: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the stop
choice_d: At least 500 feet before the stop
explanation: The manual specifies activating amber lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: When should the right turn signal be activated before pulling over for a stop?
choice_a: Only once the bus has fully stopped
choice_b: At least 500 feet before pulling over
choice_c: Immediately after activating the amber lights
choice_d: About 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over
explanation: The manual instructs turning on the right turn signal about 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: When stopping to load or unload, how far away should the front bumper be from students at the designated stop?
choice_a: At least 10 feet
choice_b: At least 5 feet
choice_c: At least 20 feet
choice_d: At least 30 feet
explanation: The manual states to bring the bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: Why does the manual recommend stopping with the front bumper at least 10 feet from waiting students?
choice_a: To allow other vehicles to pass safely
choice_b: This forces students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements
choice_c: To comply with railroad crossing regulations
choice_d: To reduce brake wear
explanation: The manual explains this distance forces students to walk to the bus, giving the driver a better view of their movements.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: At each stop, what should the driver do with the transmission?
choice_a: Leave it in Drive with foot on the brake
choice_b: Shift to a lower gear only
choice_c: Place it in Park, or Neutral if there is no Park shift point, and set the parking brake
choice_d: Turn off the engine without shifting
explanation: The manual states to place the transmission in Park (or Neutral if there is no Park shift point) and set the parking brake at each stop.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: Before completely opening the door and signaling students to approach, the driver should:
choice_a: Sound the horn twice
choice_b: Turn off the engine
choice_c: Release the parking brake
choice_d: Make a final check to see that all traffic has stopped
explanation: The manual requires a final check that all traffic has stopped before completely opening the door and signaling students.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.1 - Approaching the Stop

question: During loading, when should students board the bus?
choice_a: Only when signaled by the driver
choice_b: As soon as the bus comes to a stop
choice_c: In any order they choose, without a signal
choice_d: Before the driver checks mirrors
explanation: The manual states students should board the bus only when signaled by the driver.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: What should be turned on while students are loading in the dark?
choice_a: The strobe light only
choice_b: The dome light
choice_c: The heater
choice_d: The four-way flashers only
explanation: The manual states the dome light should be on while loading in the dark.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: If the driver cannot account for a student outside the bus during loading, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Continue the route and report it at the next stop
choice_b: Sound the horn repeatedly until the student appears
choice_c: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
choice_d: Ask a passing motorist to search for the student
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.2 - Loading Procedures

question: During unloading on the route, students should exit and walk at least how far from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see them?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 15 feet
choice_c: 20 feet
choice_d: 10 feet
explanation: The manual states students should walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see them.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: Why should the driver count the number of students while unloading?
choice_a: To confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop
choice_b: To record attendance for the school office
choice_c: To calculate remaining route time
choice_d: To determine how much fuel remains
explanation: The manual instructs counting students while unloading to confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: If a driver realizes they have missed a student's unloading stop, what should they do?
choice_a: Immediately back up to the correct stop
choice_b: Not back up, and follow local procedures
choice_c: Turn around at the next available intersection
choice_d: Radio the student's parents from the bus
explanation: The manual states if you have missed a student's unloading stop, do not back up, and be sure to follow local procedures.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When a student must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, how far in front of the right corner of the bumper should they walk before crossing, while remaining away from the front of the bus?
choice_a: At least 5 feet
choice_b: At least 20 feet
choice_c: At least 10 feet
choice_d: At least 15 feet
explanation: The manual states students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When a student reaches the edge of the roadway to cross in front of the bus, the student should first:
choice_a: Cross immediately if the bus has stopped
choice_b: Signal to oncoming traffic
choice_c: Wave to the driver
choice_d: Stop and look in all directions, making sure the roadway is clear and safe
explanation: The manual states students should stop and look in all directions, making sure the roadway is clear and safe.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: After crossing to the left edge of the school bus, a student should:
choice_a: Stop and look again for the driver's signal before continuing to cross
choice_b: Continue walking without stopping
choice_c: Wait for the alternating red lights to turn off
choice_d: Run to the other side of the road
explanation: The manual states students should stop at the left edge of the school bus and look again for the driver's signal to continue crossing.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.3 - Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: During a post-trip inspection, the driver should walk through and around the bus looking for all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_a: Sleeping students
choice_b: Fuel tank pressure readings
choice_c: Open windows and doors
choice_d: Articles left on the bus
explanation: Post-trip inspection checks for left articles, sleeping students, open windows/doors, and mechanical/operational problems; fuel tank pressure is not a listed item.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.6 - Post-trip Inspection

question: If a student drops an object near the bus during loading or unloading, the student should be told to:
choice_a: Retrieve it immediately before boarding
choice_b: Ask another student to pick it up
choice_c: Leave the object and move to a point of safety, then try to get the driver's attention
choice_d: Wait next to the object until the driver notices
explanation: The manual states students should leave dropped objects, move to a point of safety, and attempt to get the driver's attention to retrieve the object.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.5 - Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

question: "Handrail hang-ups" refers to the danger of:
choice_a: The handrail breaking under weight
choice_b: Students climbing over the handrail
choice_c: The handrail interfering with the door sensor
choice_d: Clothing, accessories, or body parts getting caught in the handrail or door while exiting
explanation: The manual warns that students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or body parts get caught in the handrail or door as they exit.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.5 - Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

question: When students exit at school in an orderly fashion, the driver should observe them to confirm that:
choice_a: All move promptly away from the unloading area
choice_b: They form a single-file line at the entrance
choice_c: They return to collect items left behind
choice_d: They wait near the bus until it departs
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to observe students as they step from the bus to see that all move promptly away from the unloading area.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.2.4 - Unloading Procedures at School

question: If time permits, what should a school bus driver do before deciding to evacuate the bus?
choice_a: Evacuate immediately as a precaution
choice_b: Contact the dispatcher to explain the situation
choice_c: Wait for a police officer to arrive
choice_d: Call the parents of all students
explanation: The manual states that if time permits, drivers should contact their dispatcher to explain the situation before deciding to evacuate.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: As a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by:
choice_a: Evacuating the bus immediately in any emergency
choice_b: Allowing students to decide individually whether to evacuate
choice_c: Keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk
choice_d: Sending the oldest student to find help before doing anything else
explanation: The manual states student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus if it does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition to consider before deciding to evacuate a school bus?
choice_a: Whether the route is behind schedule
choice_b: Whether students have completed their homework
choice_c: Whether the bus needs refueling soon
choice_d: Whether there is a fire or danger of fire
explanation: The manual lists fire or danger of fire as one of several conditions to weigh before deciding to evacuate.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: Which situation requires a MANDATORY evacuation of the school bus?
choice_a: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_b: A student reports feeling carsick
choice_c: The bus is running behind schedule
choice_d: The air conditioning has stopped working
explanation: The manual lists a bus stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing as a mandatory evacuation situation.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.1 - Planning for Emergencies

question: A safe place for evacuated students should be located how far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic?
choice_a: At least 50 feet
choice_b: At least 100 feet
choice_c: At least 150 feet
choice_d: At least 250 feet
explanation: The manual states a safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: If there is a risk from a spilled hazardous material, students should be led upwind of the bus at least how many feet?
choice_a: 100 feet
choice_b: 200 feet
choice_c: 300 feet
choice_d: 500 feet
explanation: The manual states to lead students upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: If fire is present during an evacuation, which direction should students be led?
choice_a: Downwind of the bus
choice_b: Toward the fire to assess it
choice_c: Directly behind the bus
choice_d: Upwind of the bus
explanation: The manual states to lead students upwind of the bus if fire is present.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: If a tornado is sighted, evacuation is ordered, and no building shelter is available, students should be directed to:
choice_a: Lie face down in a nearby ditch or culvert with hands covering their heads
choice_b: Remain seated on the bus with seatbelts fastened
choice_c: Stand close together next to the bus for shelter
choice_d: Run toward the nearest building regardless of distance
explanation: The manual instructs escorting students to a nearby ditch or culvert and directing them to lie face down with hands covering their heads, far enough away that the bus cannot topple on them.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: When securing the bus before an evacuation, which of these is NOT a step listed in the manual?
choice_a: Setting the parking brakes
choice_b: Accelerating away from the scene
choice_c: Shutting off the engine
choice_d: Removing the ignition key
explanation: Securing the bus involves setting the parking brakes, shutting off the engine, removing the ignition key, and activating hazard-warning lights, not driving away.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: Should a driver move a student believed to have a neck or spinal injury during an evacuation?
choice_a: Yes, always move them to the exit first
choice_b: Only if a parent gives phone permission
choice_c: No, unless his or her life is in immediate danger
choice_d: Only after calling 911 first
explanation: The manual states do not move a student believed to have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.3.2 - Evacuation Procedures

question: A "passive" railroad-highway crossing is one that:
choice_a: Has flashing red lights and gates
choice_b: Is only used during school hours
choice_c: Has a police officer stationed at all times
choice_d: Does not have any type of traffic control device
explanation: The manual defines a passive crossing as one that does not have any type of traffic control device.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.1 - Types of Crossings

question: At a passive railroad crossing, the decision to proceed rests:
choice_a: Entirely in the driver's hands
choice_b: With the dispatcher
choice_c: With the school district transportation office
choice_d: With a crossing guard
explanation: The manual states the decision to proceed rests entirely in the driver's hands at passive crossings.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.1 - Types of Crossings

question: The round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign before a railroad crossing tells the driver to:
choice_a: Stop immediately regardless of conditions
choice_b: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop
choice_c: Speed up to clear the crossing before a train arrives
choice_d: Activate the stop arm
explanation: The manual states the advance warning sign tells the driver to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: A cross-buck sign at a railroad crossing requires the driver to:
choice_a: Proceed without stopping if no train is visible
choice_b: Only stop if flashing lights are active
choice_c: Yield the right-of-way to the train
choice_d: Ignore it if a white stop line is absent
explanation: The manual states the cross-buck sign requires the driver to yield the right-of-way to the train.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.2 - Warning Signs and Devices

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, the driver should activate hazard lights approximately how far before the crossing?
choice_a: 50 feet
choice_b: 100 feet
choice_c: 500 feet
choice_d: 200 feet
explanation: The manual instructs activating hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: At a railroad crossing, the driver should stop no closer than how many feet from the nearest rail?
choice_a: 15 feet
choice_b: 5 feet
choice_c: 25 feet
choice_d: 35 feet
explanation: The manual states to stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: At a railroad crossing, the driver should stop no farther than how many feet from the nearest rail?
choice_a: 25 feet
choice_b: 50 feet
choice_c: 75 feet
choice_d: 100 feet
explanation: The manual states to stop no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where the driver has the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: After stopping at a railroad crossing, why should the driver open the service door and driver's window?
choice_a: To allow students to check for a train
choice_b: To cool down the interior of the bus
choice_c: To look and listen for an approaching train
choice_d: To signal other traffic that the bus is stopped
explanation: The manual instructs opening the service door and driver's window, then looking and listening for an approaching train.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: At a multiple-track crossing, where should the driver stop?
choice_a: Before each individual track in sequence
choice_b: Only after crossing all tracks
choice_c: There is no requirement to stop at multi-track crossings
choice_d: Only before the first set of tracks
explanation: The manual states that at a multiple-track crossing, the driver should stop only before the first set of tracks.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: While crossing railroad tracks, the driver should:
choice_a: Cross in a low gear and not change gears while crossing
choice_b: Shift to a higher gear to clear quickly
choice_c: Come to a complete stop while straddling the tracks
choice_d: Accelerate rapidly regardless of gear
explanation: The manual instructs crossing the tracks in a low gear and not changing gears while crossing.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: If the crossing gate comes down after the bus has already started across the tracks, the driver should:
choice_a: Stop immediately on the tracks and wait
choice_b: Drive through the gate even if it means breaking it
choice_c: Back up off the tracks
choice_d: Wait for the gate to rise before proceeding
explanation: The manual states if the gate comes down after you have started across, drive through it even if it means breaking the gate.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.3 - Recommended Procedures

question: If a school bus stalls or becomes trapped on railroad tracks, the driver should:
choice_a: Remain on the bus and radio for help
choice_b: Attempt to restart the engine before evacuating
choice_c: Get everyone out and move away from the bus at an angle, away from the tracks and toward the train
choice_d: Move all students to the rear of the bus
explanation: The manual states to get everyone out immediately and move away from the bus at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.4 - Special Situations

question: As a general rule for determining an acceptable containment/storage area at a crossing, how many feet should be added to the length of the school bus?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: 10 feet
choice_c: 20 feet
choice_d: 15 feet
explanation: The manual states to add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.4.4 - Special Situations

question: When should a driver address an on-bus behavior problem, according to the manual?
choice_a: After the unloading students are safely off the bus and moved away, or by pulling the bus over
choice_b: Immediately while continuing to drive and load/unload
choice_c: Only after completing the entire route
choice_d: By radioing the school office while still driving
explanation: The manual advises waiting until students are safely off and moved away, or pulling the bus over if necessary, since loading/unloading requires full concentration.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.5.1 - Don't Deal with On-bus Problems When Loading and Unloading

question: Where should a driver never put a student off the bus when handling a serious discipline problem?
choice_a: At the student's designated school bus stop
choice_b: Anywhere except at school or the student's designated school bus stop
choice_c: At school
choice_d: Nowhere is off-limits if the offense is serious enough
explanation: The manual states to never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.5.2 - Handling Serious Problems

question: Federal requirements mandate ABS on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, converter dollies) built on or after:
choice_a: March 1, 1995
choice_b: March 1, 2000
choice_c: March 1, 1998
choice_d: March 1, 2005
explanation: The manual states air brake vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998 are required to have ABS.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.6.1 - Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Hydraulically braked buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more require ABS if built on or after:
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: March 1, 1998
choice_c: March 1, 2001
choice_d: March 1, 1999
explanation: The manual states hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999 require ABS.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.6.1 - Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: In an emergency braking situation on a bus equipped with ABS, the driver should:
choice_a: Not pump the brakes
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly
choice_c: Release the brakes completely and coast
choice_d: Shift into neutral before braking
explanation: The manual states that in emergency braking, the driver should not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.6.3 - Braking with ABS

question: Which statement about ABS is TRUE according to the manual?
choice_a: ABS allows the driver to follow more closely
choice_b: ABS will help maintain vehicle control but will not necessarily shorten stopping distance
choice_c: ABS prevents all skids, including those from spinning drive wheels
choice_d: ABS increases the ultimate stopping power of the brakes
explanation: The manual states ABS will help maintain vehicle control, but will not always shorten stopping distance, and is an add-on, not a replacement for normal brakes.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.6.5 - Safety Reminders

topic: Braking if ABS is Not Working
question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check, or comes on while driving, this indicates:
choice_a: The service brakes have failed completely
choice_b: The transmission needs immediate service
choice_c: The driver may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels
choice_d: The parking brake is engaged
explanation: The manual states if the lamp stays on after the bulb check or goes on once underway, the driver may have lost ABS control at one or more wheels.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.6.4 - Braking if ABS is Not Working

topic: Braking if ABS is Not Working
question: If a bus's ABS malfunctions, the driver:
choice_a: Loses all braking ability immediately
choice_b: Must stop the bus and evacuate students at once
choice_c: Cannot legally continue driving the route
choice_d: Still has regular brakes and should drive normally but get the system serviced soon
explanation: The manual states that if ABS malfunctions, the driver still has regular brakes and should drive normally, but get the system serviced soon.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.6.4 - Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: Roof-mounted white strobe lights on a school bus should be used when:
choice_a: The driver has limited visibility
choice_b: Loading and unloading students at every stop
choice_c: Driving at night regardless of visibility conditions
choice_d: Approaching any railroad crossing
explanation: The manual states the overhead strobe light should be used when the driver has limited visibility.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.7.1 - Strobe Lights

question: According to the manual, why do strong winds significantly affect a school bus?
choice_a: Because the bus has an unusually low center of gravity
choice_b: Because the side of the bus acts like a sail on a sailboat, and wind can push it sideways or tip it over
choice_c: Because wind only affects the braking system
choice_d: Because school buses have no wind resistance rating
explanation: The manual compares the side of a school bus to a sail on a sailboat; strong winds can push the bus sideways or, in extreme conditions, tip it over.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.7.2 - Driving in High Winds

question: According to the manual, backing a school bus is:
choice_a: Encouraged as the safest way to reposition the bus
choice_b: Prohibited under all circumstances without exception
choice_c: Strongly discouraged and should be done only when there is no other safe way to move the vehicle
choice_d: Permitted only when students remain seated on board
explanation: The manual states backing a school bus is strongly discouraged, and the driver should back the bus only when there is no other safe way to move it.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.7.3 - Backing

question: What is the maximum tail swing a school bus can have?
choice_a: One foot
choice_b: Five feet
choice_c: Two feet
choice_d: Three feet
explanation: The manual states a school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, so drivers should check mirrors during turning movements.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 10.7.4 - Tail Swing
